sup-2c216485e9c9ddff-q3:whole.hint: When speed is constant, compare the total distance with the rate of covering it.
notes: For uniform motion, distance = speed × time. Use the speed of light in vacuum when the question describes light travelling through space.
Convert the distance to compatible units first, and convert the final time to the unit used in the choices.

sup-4dc737acb154fbbe-q1:whole.hint: Try listing the known motion quantities first. Which constant-acceleration equation leaves only the quantity you need?
notes: For constant acceleration, use v = u + at, s = ut + ½at² or v² = u² + 2as. Choose the equation that avoids an unknown you do not need.
Choose one positive direction and keep the signs of displacement, velocity and acceleration consistent. Speed is the magnitude of velocity.

sup-4dc737acb154fbbe-q2:whole.hint: Read both axis labels before using the graph. Are you looking for a gradient or an area?
notes: On a displacement–time graph, gradient gives velocity. On a velocity–time graph, gradient gives acceleration and signed area gives displacement.
On an acceleration–time graph, area gives the change in velocity; add the initial velocity. Distance travelled requires the magnitudes of the velocity–time areas.
